comparisons.reason: Both are any-comment binary features over OC_comments, but the constructs differ. Feature 0 requires a specific real-world example (an identifiable event, person, case, organization, place or product) cited in support of an argument. Feature 1 requires specific factual data (statistics, figures, dates) or verifiable citations (links, named sources, laws). A comment can give a named example with no data or citation, such as naming a historical event or a company. A comment can also give a statistic or a law citation without a particular real-world case. The overlap is partial, so the eligibility rules differ materially.
